summary: The legal input cap produces too few output digits for stable runtime scaling, while the output length itself gives a logarithmic lower bound matched by repeated division.

optimality.argument: The base-16 representation of n squared and base-36 representation of n cubed together contain Theta(log n) symbols that every correct algorithm must emit. Repeated division produces each symbol with constant arithmetic work and therefore matches that lower bound.

replacement_checks.evidence: The returned string contains Theta(log n) base digits, and producing that many output symbols requires Omega(log n) time.
Each helper iteration divides by its fixed base and emits one digit, so both conversions finish in O(log n) total iterations.
Authored cases cover the minimum and maximum inputs, sample values, both numeral-place boundaries, digit-to-letter transitions, and multi-digit outputs.
